notes: The document's coding table has no code for partial hip resurfacing (S2118 is metal-on-metal total resurfacing), so this pathway is tied to no listed code.

notes: Built from the PDF only (02-20000-50, Reviewed 01/23/25, Revised 02/15/25). The download holds a single clean copy; there is no redline. effective_date is the printed Revised date of this version (the Original Effective Date 10/15/16 is the first version); reviewed_date is the printed Reviewed date. pdftotext drops the bullet glyphs in this PDF; the indentation still shows the nesting.

THA list structure: '1 or more of the following conditions exist' is six single indications joined by OR, then a compound seventh: 'Advanced joint disease ... AND' with 'Pain or functional disability ...' and 'Failure of at least 3 months of conservative non-surgical management ...' indented as sub-bullets beneath it. Pain/disability and the conservative trial therefore attach only to the advanced-joint-disease alternative, not to the malignancy, AVN, fracture, failed-surgery or mal-union alternatives. Tree: any(6 single indications, all(advanced disease, pain/disability, conservative trial)).

'No contraindications* to total hip arthroplasty for any indication above are present' is indented like the conservative-management modalities but 'for any indication above' makes it a general requirement for every THA alternative; modelled as not(any(the four starred contraindications)) in the THA pathway's all. 'No contraindications* to revision arthroplasty are present' is modelled the same way in the Revision pathway. Those two sentences are not criteria; the four contraindication items are, and the ids are shared by both pathways.

Conservative management: the criterion is the 3-month documented trial (duration_months >= 3) and the seven modalities are an any() beneath it ('includes 1 or more of the following'); unlike the knee guideline, therapeutic injections are not listed for the hip. The hip PDF reads 'and that includes'; the criterion text stops before that clause so it is the requirement's exact words.

Metal-on-metal total hip resurfacing: 'Is a candidate for total hip replacement' is kept as one leaf (what a surgeon documents) rather than nesting the whole THA tree; a stricter reviewer could substitute the THA pathway's requirements for this leaf. 'Is likely to outlive a traditional prosthesis (eg, age 55 or younger)' is one leaf with an age threshold <= 55 years; the 'eg' makes 55 an example, not a hard cutoff, so an older patient documented as likely to outlive a prosthesis could still satisfy it.

Resurfacing contraindication 'Severely overweight (without attempted weight loss or discussion of increased risk related to BMI)' holds an embedded waiver: it is a contraindication only when the patient is severely overweight AND neither attempted weight loss nor a BMI-risk discussion is documented. Modelled inside the contraindication any() as all(severely overweight, not(any(attempted weight loss, discussion of increased risk related to BMI))), so that either waiver clears it. The three parts are separate criteria with the PDF's exact substrings.

Partial hip resurfacing (hardest call): the bullet 'Has known or suspected metal sensitivity or concern about potential effects of metal ions' carries no AND/OR connector in the PDF while every other bullet in the list ends with AND. We read it as a required element (all of five bullets plus the population qualifier 'osteonecrosis of the femoral head'), since the list is otherwise conjunctive and partial resurfacing is positioned as the option for patients who cannot have a metal-on-metal total resurfacing. The same criterion id (hr_metal_sensitivity) is a contraindication for total resurfacing and a requirement for partial resurfacing; the verbatim text 'Known or suspected metal sensitivity or concern about potential effects of metal ions' is the substring common to both bullets.

Partial hip resurfacing thresholds: 'There is no more than 50% involvement of the femoral head' is number <= 50 (kept as a positive leaf rather than not(the total-resurfacing contraindication 'more than 50% involvement'), since the PDF states it as its own positive requirement). 'Multiple cysts of the femoral head (>1 cm)' is number > 1 cm; 'more than 50% involvement' is number > 50.

Code-to-pathway mapping: the coding table does not tie codes to sections. 27130 (total hip arthroplasty) -> Total hip arthroplasty; 27132 (conversion of previous hip surgery to total hip arthroplasty) -> Total hip arthroplasty, because the THA indications 'Failure of previous hip surgery' and 'Mal-union of acetabular or proximal femur fracture' describe a conversion, and the Revision indications all concern an existing implant; 27134, 27137, 27138 (revision of total hip arthroplasty) -> Revision arthroplasty; S2118 (metal-on-metal total hip resurfacing) -> Metal-on-metal total hip resurfacing. Partial hip resurfacing has no code in the table, so its applies_to_cpt is empty: under the app's rule that an untied pathway governs only codes no other pathway names, it governs none of the six listed codes; under the brief's 'empty list = all codes' reading it would be checked for every order, which is a leniency we flag here. A reviewer could instead attach it to S2118.

Exclusion: 'All other types and applications of hip resurfacing are considered experimental or investigational.' names no code; S2118 itself is the covered metal-on-metal total resurfacing, so the exclusion's cpt list is empty. No listed code is non-covered or investigational.

Bullets that hold alternatives with 'or' inside an OR list ('Fracture or mechanical failure of the implant', 'Recurrent or irreducible dislocation', 'Progressive or substantial bone loss', 'Instability of one or both components') are kept as one criterion each, since splitting them inside an any() changes nothing. 'Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis of femoral head)' is one criterion; 'avascular necrosis' also appears inside the advanced-joint-disease imaging list, copied with the PDF's stray closing parenthesis.

Program exceptions: FEP and SAO follow their own guidelines; Medicare Advantage products: the LCD Major Joint Replacement (Hip and Knee) L33618 'was reviewed on the last guideline review date', which we read (as the hand-built varicose vein fixture does) as Medicare Advantage following the LCD rather than this guideline.

Left out of the tree: the DESCRIPTION section (including 'Partial hip resurfacing is considered a treatment option for avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head' and the named metal-on-metal devices) because it is background, not the position statement; the guideline update history; the related guidelines list.
